mcat_description.short: Prefabricated accommodation refers to factory-built, modular housing structures designed for temporary or semi-permanent use at construction sites, industrial projects, and remote locations, typically assembled from steel frames and insulated sandwich panels (PUF/EPS/Rockwool) and sold per unit or per sq ft.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated accommodation units are off-site manufactured, relocatable housing structures built using cold-formed or mild steel frames with insulated sandwich panel walls and roofs, designed to provide safe, hygienic, and functional living quarters for workers, staff, and labour at construction sites, mining areas, infrastructure projects, and industrial campuses across India. These structures are available as single-storey portable cabins, multi-storey labour colonies (G+1, G+2), and container-converted accommodation units, and can be customised with bunk beds, attached bathrooms, kitchens, electrical fittings, and sanitation systems. Built to IS-grade material standards and compliant with National Building Code (NBC) guidelines for prefabricated construction, they offer rapid installation (days to weeks), easy dismantling, and multi-site reusability — making them the preferred alternative to conventional brick-and-mortar worker housing for EPC contractors, infrastructure developers, and industrial operators. The dominant panel materials in the Indian market are PUF (polyurethane foam) sandwich panels and glass wool/EPS insulated panels, with mild steel or GI structural frames.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, prefabricated accommodation is primarily understood as factory-built, relocatable worker and labour housing structures used at construction sites, infrastructure projects, and industrial campuses — distinct from permanent prefab homes or luxury modular villas. The dominant construction method uses mild steel or GI structural frames with PUF (polyurethane foam) or EPS/Rockwool insulated sandwich panels, with 50mm panel thickness being a common specification. Leading Indian manufacturers include EPACK Prefab (K-House system), Pressmach Infrastructure, Epsilon Enterprise (Ahmedabad), and Hind Portable Cabin (Thane/Ahmedabad), with manufacturing hubs concentrated in Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Thane (Maharashtra), and Faridabad (Haryana). Structures are available as single-storey portable cabins, G+1 and G+2 multi-storey labour colonies, and container-converted accommodation units (20ft and 40ft), with customisation for bunk beds, attached bathrooms, kitchens, and electrical/sanitation fit-outs. The relevant Indian standards framework includes IS 15917:2010 (Building Design and Erection Using Prefabricated Systems — mixed/composite construction) and IS 15916:2010 (prefabricated concrete), with structural design governed by IS 1893 for seismic loads; the National Building Code (NBC) by BIS provides overarching guidelines for prefabricated construction in India. Buyers are predominantly EPC contractors, infrastructure developers, and industrial operators who prioritise rapid deployment (days to weeks), multi-site reusability, and compliance with worker welfare norms; government and PSU buyers additionally require fire safety and seismic resistance certifications.
